record.original_question: For a uniformly random 3-regular graph on n vertices, let E(theta) = (1/2) sum_{i,j=1}^n Aij(1 - cos(theta_i - theta_j)) where A is the adjacency matrix, and call the graph globally synchronizing when all local minima of E are global minima corresponding to constant phase vectors theta_i = c. Is it true that a uniform random 3-regular graph is globally synchronizing with high probability as n -> infinity?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3 (Globally Synchronizing Regular Graphs). A uniform random 3-regular graph is globally synchronizing with high probability (probability going to 1 as n → ∞).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on vertex set $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with adjacency matrix $A=(A_{ij})$. For phase angles $\theta=(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n$, define the energy
$$E(\theta)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}A_{ij}\bigl(1-\cos(\theta_i-\theta_j)\bigr).$$
Call $G$ "globally synchronizing" if every local minimum of $E$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^n$ is a global minimum, i.e.\ corresponds to a constant phase vector $\theta_i=c$ for all $i$ (so that $E=0$).

Let $G_n$ be a uniformly random 3-regular graph on $n$ vertices (sampled from the set of all simple 3-regular graphs on $n$ labelled vertices, for $n$ even).

Prove or disprove: as $n\to\infty$,
$$\Pr\bigl(G_n\text{ is globally synchronizing}\bigr)\longrightarrow 1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be open. Recent work (Abdalla–Bandeira–Kassabov–Souza–Strogatz–Townsend, "Expander graphs are globally synchronizing", 2022) establishes global synchronization for random d-regular graphs only for sufficiently large d (d ≥ 600), and a 2025 paper shows the random graph process is globally synchronizing, but the sparse case d = 3 remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Expander graphs are globally synchronizing
status_evidence.snippet: Shows uniform d-regular graphs are globally synchronizing w.h.p. for d ≥ 600; the case of small d (including d=3) is left open.
status_evidence.claim: Result for large d only; 3-regular case open.

status_evidence.title: The random graph process is globally synchronizing
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes global synchronization for the Erdős–Rényi random graph process; does not resolve the random 3-regular conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related progress, but 3-regular conjecture not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Global Synchronization (problems 3-5) | Randomstrasse 101
status_evidence.snippet: Lists global synchronization of random 3-regular graphs as an open problem.
